# Neonix

> Neonix is an HTML-to-motion-video compiler: it turns HTML and CSS into a real, exportable motion video.

Neonix is an HTML-to-motion-video compiler. Users — or AI agents like Claude,
ChatGPT, and Grok, connected over Remote MCP — write HTML and CSS describing
a scene. Neonix validates and compiles it into a canonical motion-video
document (Neonix Protocol V2), then renders it to a real, exportable MP4. It
is not a template generator or a prompt-only video tool.

## FAQ

Q: What is Neonix?
A: Neonix is an HTML-to-motion-video compiler that turns HTML and CSS into a
real, exportable video.

Q: How do AI agents use Neonix?
A: AI agents such as Claude connect to Neonix's Remote MCP server
(www.neonix.video/api/mcp) and call tools like create_project_html to compile
HTML/CSS into a video project, then export it as MP4.

Q: What makes Neonix different from template-based AI video tools?
A: Neonix compiles arbitrary HTML/CSS into a canonical protocol document and
renders it deterministically — it does not fill in a fixed template.

Q: Can Neonix convert HTML/CSS to MP4?
A: Yes. Neonix compiles HTML/CSS into Neonix Protocol V2, then exports MP4
through its native render pipeline.

Q: How does Neonix's pipeline work?
A: Neonix compiles HTML/CSS into Neonix Protocol V2 (JSON), which you can
preview and edit in the Neonix editor, then export to a real MP4.
